name: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard
summary: Posture recovery from Crackhead Control opens the two-leg high clinch before the top player rebuilds upright posture inside the remaining guard.
description: Posture recovery from Crackhead Control opens the two-leg high clinch before the top player rebuilds upright posture inside the remaining guard.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The top player must free the shoulder line first; a high clinch is not safely defeated by suddenly standing or stacking.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): How do you avoid offering an arm-lock lever?
flashcards.answer: Keep the elbows compact while addressing the high clinch instead of straightening them to force posture.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep the elbow compact in high guard

plausible: Straight arm between both high legs
Hand reaching far behind them
trap: Pull wrist with shoulder still held

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): What reinforces Crackhead's restriction on your head?
flashcards.answer: The added high leg reinforces upper-body posture control; the lower guard must be assessed separately after release.
flashcards.answer_line: The second leg rising behind it

plausible: Low ankle crossing at your waist
Foot on your hip below the elbow
trap: High foot beside shoulder, head free

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): What can preserve space before high closure?
flashcards.answer: Early inside frames manage the hip line before the upper-body clinch closes tightly.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside hip or thigh frame and base

plausible: Wrist grip without thigh contact
Outside thigh push with elbow flared

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): How do you create slack without twisting a trapped arm?
flashcards.answer: Create space at the hip and thigh with the head and arm aligned, then use the released opening.
flashcards.answer_line: Head/arm aligned as hip space opens

plausible: Turn torso away from the held elbow
Pull hand behind hip before release
trap: Lift head before upper arm follows

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): What must happen before the shoulder withdraws?
flashcards.answer: Clear both the high-leg connection and any upper-arm overhook before withdrawing the shoulder and elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: The high legs and overhook must open

plausible: Only the second high leg lowers
Only their lower ankles open
trap: Only your chin rises above the shin

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): Upright with shoulders free, what confirms closed guard?
flashcards.answer: After upper-body clearance, closed guard exists only if the bottom player's legs reclose lower around the torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Their ankles close below your waist

plausible: High legs retain both of your arms
Both knees passed; chest beside ribs
trap: Ankles apart with one leg under arm

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): What body region is trapped at the start?
flashcards.answer: This recovery starts inside Crackhead's upper-body clinch, not solely a low leg entanglement.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and shoulders in the high legs

plausible: Only waist in a low ankle crossing
Only wrist below free shoulders
trap: Only elbow beneath legs at the hips

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): Why is getting your chin higher insufficient?
flashcards.answer: Confirm shoulder and arm freedom before interpreting head movement as recovered posture.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder or overhook may stay caught

plausible: Elbow follows chin out of the legs
Head height proves knee hug has slid
trap: Head upright means overhook is gone

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): Why avoid suddenly standing against the clinch?
flashcards.answer: Sudden elevation through the retained enclosure is not controlled release; clear the upper connection first.
flashcards.answer_line: Retained legs can load neck and arm

plausible: Standing opens clinch before loading
Knee hug slides off as you stand

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (top): What still separates recovered posture from a guard pass?
flashcards.answer: Upright posture inside closed guard leaves the lower guard to address in a separate passing exchange.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower legs still encircle your torso

plausible: Only a wrist grip now blocks the pin
Low ankles open as spine straightens
trap: Head clear means hips past the knees

defender.name: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard Defender
defender.description: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (defender): Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The top player must free the shoulder line first; a high clinch is not safely defeated by suddenly standing or stacking.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees. Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again. Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

As the high legs lower, use a small hip escape behind an inside arm to return the knees around the torso. This guard retention keeps chest pressure and a crossface from pinning your shoulders while the closed guard is rebuilt.
key_principles: Start with broken posture: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg.
Bring the second leg high: Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
Track both elbows: Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.
Keep knees close: Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees.
Return to one-leg control: Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again.
Open against a stack: Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (bottom): What is retained before adding the high reinforcement?
flashcards.answer: The first high leg and its supporting hand form the foundation before the second leg reinforces it.
flashcards.answer_line: First shin held to control posture

plausible: Only feet crossed behind the waist
Only wrist grip with both knees low
trap: Neck pull with high knee unsupported

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (bottom): How should a reinforcing leg follow the opponent?
flashcards.answer: Use a comfortable hip-supported angle; release the high clinch if posture cannot be followed safely.

plausible: Drag foot with the knee still fixed
Foot held still as torso twists
trap: Foot rises while knee drifts away

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (bottom): What separates high posture control from Dead Orchard?
flashcards.answer: Check actual elbow positions and leg closure rather than equating a two-leg clinch with Dead Orchard.
flashcards.answer_line: Both arms inside a high leg triangle

plausible: Any second leg above the shoulders
Any two-arm contact below the knees
trap: One-arm triangle with far arm free

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (bottom): As the legs lower, how do you protect space for a knee?
flashcards.answer: Frame inside against chest pressure and move the hips enough to return the knees around the torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frame and a small hip escape

plausible: Both hands chase the retreating head
Move hips but leave both knees out

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery to Closed Guard (bottom): If the second high leg lowers, what remains possible?
flashcards.answer: Lowering the reinforcement can leave Mission Control; closed guard requires a separate lower leg closure.
flashcards.answer_line: Mission Control with first shin held

plausible: Closed guard with ankles still apart
Dead Orchard without a leg triangle
trap: Pass completed with first shin held
